newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Drop in Brazil TV demand prompts factory layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Drop in Brazil TV demand prompts factory layoffs.

text.p: Demand for TV sets in Brazil has dropped since March, prompting layoffs by some brown line-goods makers, but the market for the product will likely surge in 1998 ahead of the World Cup, Caspian Securities Inc said.
"The home appliances sector is revising sales estimates downwards to five percent from 10 percent as demand is lower than expected," Caspian analyst Esther Hiranobe said in a report.
But in 1998, "spurred by the World Soccer Cup, TV set demand is expected to grow by 15 percent," she added.
Electronics firms in the Amazonian city of Manaus, such as Japan's Sony and local firm CCE have laid off workers due to slackening demand for televisions since March, she said.
"Inventory levels are still high and demand has not shown any signs of recovery yet," Hiranobe said.
